newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rebound, gains seen capped.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rebound, gains seen capped.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 1.16 percent on Thursday on the back of a nine percent jump in drug wholesaler Salus, reversing a three-day losing streak, but traders remained sceptical on the market's outlook.

"I do not think that today's gains mark the beginning of a long-term uptrend. Salus went up mostly because many traders expect a good dividend to be paid this year," said Andrej Kavcic, a trader at brokers Ilirika.
The SBI index rose 15.27 points to 1,336.46.
Traders said no long-term rising trend could be expected before foreign investors return to buying.
The central bank in February blocked foreign investment by demanding international portfolio investors open special custody accounts at Slovenian banks in order to be able to trade in Slovenia.
Turnover rose to 67.2 million tolars from 45.7 million. Overall 10 shares rose, five fell and one was flat, while 11 were untraded.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded share, easing 0.20 percent to 50,700 tolars on volume of 301 shares for total turnover of 15.2 million tolars.
Salus was the top gainer, jumping 9.25 percent to 16,770 tolars on volume of 730 shares for total turnover of 11.7 million tolars.
Nobody at Salus was available for comment on market expectations of a dividend payment.
Bank Probanka led the day's decliners, falling 2.38 percent to 20,500 tolars on volume of seven shares.
